messages:
maria: FYI - ACME reported intermittent 500s and a p99 latency of ~2.1s starting 2026-03-12. Our p99 panel shows ~0.9s for the same window. Ticket #8421 includes a handful of request ids they pasted. Can we sanity-check?

jake: Thanks, passing to SRE. Do we have any correlated deploys or infra changes around 03/12?

sunita: No infra deploys for the runtime on that day. I pulled alerts: auth-service errors ticked up briefly at 03/12 04:10 UTC (spike in 401 -> client retries).

maria: Customer shared repro steps: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'` — they said ~1/100 requests returned 500 + took longer.

ops-bot: [alert] auth-service rate of 5xx increased from 0.1% -> 1.7% at 2026-03-12T04:08Z (rule: auth-5xx-spike)

jake: Two quick hypotheses: (1) client-side retries are inflating observed tail because failed auth attempts get retried with backoff -> longer total time, (2) dashboard panel is using rollup/quantile that downweights tail samples.

sunita: I ran the raw histogram query against raw spans for ACME's org-id for 03/12. Looks like there are many >1s outliers that the 1m rollup quantile function buckets into the 95th, not the true sample p99.

tyler: Also, ACME's SDK default retry is 3 retries with 500ms backoff. If auth returns transient 401/500 then overall client-observed latency = request + retry sequence. Might explain reported 2.1s.

maria: Customer insists they see 2s for single requests (not retries). They forwarded 3 request ids: `r-1734`, `r-1735`, `r-1740`. Can someone pull traces?

jake: Pulling traces now — trace `r-1734` shows service returned 200 but there is an upstream auth token refresh flow that adds ~800ms. `r-1735` includes a downstream call to key-mgmt that had a 502 for 250ms then retried. So mixed causes.

sunita: Dashboard mismatch root cause summary: our p99 panel uses a 1m rollup across hosts that drops single-host short-lived spikes; the customer's observed p99 is from raw request times (no rollup). Also bucketization: our histogram panel uses 500ms buckets, so spikes between 1.0-1.5s are grouped and the quantile math on rollups underestimates occasional tails.

tyler: Short-term mitigations: 1) ask ACME to temporarily disable client retries (or lower retries) 2) add an adhoc raw-p99 panel for org-id with 1s buckets and no rollup 3) route their traffic to a dedicated pool for the weekend if they want isolation.

maria: I sent the customer a repro checklist and asked for the raw trace ids (got two more). Also offered to disable retries server-side as a temporary experiment.

jake: Long-term actions: file ENG-1198 to change observability defaults: make p99 rollup option explicit and add docs about rollup vs sample p99; change default histogram buckets for latency to finer grain above 250ms.

sunita: I posted the query I ran in #eng-sre: ``SELECT histogram_bucket(lat_ms, 1000) AS b, count(*) FROM traces WHERE org_id='acme' AND ts >= '2026-03-12' GROUP BY b`` — this gives raw bucket counts. Recommend adding a dashboard toggle to switch to raw-histogram mode for incident triage.

tyler: I'll take ENG-1198. Quick fix PR: link: https://git.internal/redwood/obs/PR-542 (canary to staging today).

maria: I'll update ticket #8421 with findings and mitigation steps. Customer asked for ETA on a fix — gave tentative ETA of 48h for dashboard change and 1 week for defaults.

ops-bot: [incident-note] mitigation applied: org-id acme temporarily routed to dedicated pool at 2026-03-13T02:00Z; monitoring set to raw-p99 panel for next 48h.

jake: Good. Follow-up: make sure we annotate dashboards and add a tooltip explaining rollup limitations for p99.

sunita: Agreed. Adding note + runbook steps in the dashboard.

maria: Customer replied: thanks, doing A/B with retries off, seeing p99 drop to ~1.0s. They accepted the temporary routing. Closing loop after the dashboard change. :thumbsup:
